title: Deliver the HumbleStudio flagship journey v1
summary: Deliver and prove the repository flagship milestone: Deliver one polished standalone product milestone for internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace: open repository-backed product truth, edit a screen or diagram, review a proposal, hand it to Codex, and reconcile implementation. The slice must prove user value, UI/UX quality, performance, accessibility, recovery, and the declared monetization or non-monetization posture.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver the repository flagship scope as one coherent product milestone: Deliver one polished standalone product milestone for internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace: open repository-backed product truth, edit a screen or diagram, review a proposal, hand it to Codex, and reconcile implementation. The slice must prove user value, UI/UX quality, performance, accessibility, recovery, and the declared monetization or non-monetization posture.
Begin from the ratified product charter and current user problem rather than from the existing screen structure.
Define one obvious entry point, a bounded set of decisions, and a clear meaningful completion state.
Remove or defer secondary complexity that distracts from the primary outcome.
Design and implement normal, loading, empty, error, stale, offline, permission-denied, partial, retry, interruption, and recovery states.
Use repository-owned design tokens, components, content language, and interaction patterns while preserving the product identity.
Meet the repository accessibility, localization, and reduced-motion requirements.
Meet performance budgets for launch or open, the critical interaction path, memory, storage, network, and background work as applicable.
Preserve privacy, consent, credential, support, and data-lifecycle boundaries.
Make agent or automation assistance optional, transparent, reversible, and unnecessary for core value.
Apply monetization posture `internal-now-optional-commercialization-later` without dark patterns or paywalling safety, recovery, or owned data.
Capture behavior-focused tests and closest-practical runtime evidence for the complete journey.
Add an adversarial test or review that attempts to break the most important product claim.
Verify restart, replay, duplicate event, and stale-version behavior where relevant.
Define rollout or local adoption evidence and explicit safe-stop criteria.
Update user-facing documentation, support guidance, status, and product evidence after implementation.
Do not introduce unrelated cross-app integration or product merger.
Keep the implementation bounded to one reviewable roadmap milestone.
Complete zero-warning verification and record every unexecuted external gate.
Produce a post-milestone review comparing intended and observed product value.

blocked_by.reason: The capstone scope depends on reviewed earlier-wave foundations.

trigger.source_ref: Jan requested Wave 10 as the largest and most thorough final planning wave across the entire portfolio.

agent_notes: Portfolio Capstone and Operating System Wave 10.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, merge products, mutate external data, delete, restore, or enable monetization from this planning ticket.
Alternative considered and rejected: adding more disconnected ambitious features without charter, capacity, assurance, and product evidence would make the portfolio less trustworthy.
Wave 10 is a realization and rationalization layer, not a reason to keep expanding the backlog indefinitely.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `required-prerequisite`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-charter-input`, relevance `next`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `use as governing context, not another parallel backlog`. Portfolio and product charters remain decision inputs, while Wave 11 and Wave 12 own implementation and completion.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-product-charter-input` / `next` / priority `high`. Product role, lifecycle, and investment decisions frame the validation program.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid`; publication `publish-after-fresh-reconciliation`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Product role, lifecycle, and investment decisions frame the validation program.
